en.title: American Airlines swaps its 84-mile South Bend bus for CRJ-700 jets — and halves departures
en.summary: American Airlines has replaced the Landline motorcoach between South Bend and Chicago O'Hare with three daily Bombardier CRJ-700 round trips, cutting blocked time from about 2 hours 45 minutes to about 1 hour 15 minutes. Fares start at about $239 one way, well below the bus's reported peak of $1,280, but departures are fewer than in the bus era, while Rockford's bus ended with no replacement.
body: American Airlines has replaced buses with jets on the 84-mile (135 km) link between South Bend Regional Airport in Indiana and Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD), switching to the aircraft link in October 2026, according to WNDU. Under the Landline arrangement, passengers checked in at the small airport, cleared TSA screening there and rode to a secure-side gate at O'Hare, with bags checked through to the final destination, and the coach carried a flight number and earned AAdvantage miles. The new service is operated by SkyWest Airlines as American Eagle with dual-class Bombardier CRJ-700 regional jets, offering three daily round trips and a blocked time of about 1 hour 15 minutes, roughly an hour and a half less than the bus.

The trade-off is frequency: daily seats ease only from 210 to 195, but travelers have fewer departure choices, and United Airlines operates up to eight daily round trips on the route, compared with American's three. South Bend Regional Airport CEO Mike Daigle said the connection was in high demand and now offers one-stop access to more than 350 destinations. Rockford, whose bus launched around the same time in October 2025, fared worse: Chicago Rockford International Airport (RFD) was told on July 31, 2026 that service would end October 4, passengers were offered refunds or alternate arrangements, and no replacement flights followed, leaving Rockford without its only link to American. The Philadelphia Landline partnership continues, linking five regional airports to that hub.

facts.claim: American Airlines switched the South Bend–O'Hare Landline motorcoach link to an aircraft link in October 2026, according to WNDU.

The new service offers three daily round trips on dual-class Bombardier CRJ-700 jets operated by SkyWest Airlines as American Eagle, with a blocked time of about 1 hour 15 minutes versus about 2 hours 45 minutes for the bus, and daily seats easing from 210 to 195.
One-way bus fares reached as high as $1,280, while the new jet service starts at about $239 one way.

Landline launched at O'Hare in October 2025 with South Bend and Rockford spokes; passengers checked in at the small airport, cleared TSA screening there, rode to a secure-side gate at O'Hare, and had bags checked through, with the coach carrying a flight number and earning AAdvantage miles.

Chicago Rockford International Airport was informed on July 31, 2026 that its motorcoach service would end October 4; passengers were offered refunds or alternate arrangements and no replacement flights followed, leaving Rockford without its only link to American.

United Airlines operates up to eight daily round trips on the route compared with American's three, and South Bend Regional Airport CEO Mike Daigle said the connection was in high demand and offers one-stop access to more than 350 destinations.

zh.title: 美航南本德—芝加哥84英里接駁改由CRJ-700執飛、班次減半
zh.summary: 美國航空10月起以龐巴迪CRJ-700噴射機取代南本德與芝加哥歐海爾機場之間的Landline巴士接駁，航程僅84英里、每日3班往返；單程票價約239美元起，遠低於巴士時期最高1280美元，但出發選擇少於巴士時期；同於2025年10月啟用的羅克福德巴士則直接停駛、未獲替代航班。
body: 美國航空已把印第安納州南本德地區機場與芝加哥歐海爾國際機場之間的接駁，從Landline巴士改為噴射機。根據WNDU報導，這項轉換於2026年10月生效；巴士時期旅客在小型機場報到、通過安檢後搭車前往歐海爾機場管制區內的登機門，行李可直掛最終目的地，巴士本身還帶有航班編號並可累積哩程。這條僅84英里（135公里）的路線改由天西航空以美國之鷹名義執飛的龐巴迪CRJ-700執飛，每日3班往返，飛行時間約1小時15分鐘，較巴士約2小時45分鐘省下約一個半小時。

班次減少是這次轉換的代價：每日座位數由巴士時期的210個微降至195個，但出發選擇明顯變少；相較之下，聯合航空在同一市場每日最多提供8班往返。南本德地區機場執行長Mike Daigle表示，這條航線需求強勁，經歐海爾轉機能一站通往350多個目的地。另一方面，與南本德同於2025年10月啟用的羅克福德巴士則在不到一年後停駛：機場於2026年7月31日獲知10月4日為最後營運日，旅客可退票或改訂其他安排，且沒有替代航班，羅克福德等於失去與美航的唯一連結。美航在費城的Landline巴士合作仍持續，連結5座地區機場。
